units.response:
Decision: UNRESOLVED

The Council recorded two distinct votes regarding Mali sanctions. On S/2023/638, France and the UAE proposed renewing sanctions and extending the Panel of Experts. The draft received 13 votes in favor, 1 against (Russia), and 1 abstention (China). France supported the measure, citing the need to support the peace agreement and orderly drawdown, while the UAE acknowledged the transitional government's request to lift sanctions. Russia cast the sole negative vote, arguing the existing approach failed to address Mali's concerns. Consequently, the draft was not adopted.

Separately, Russia submitted S/2023/639 for a final extension and immediate dissolution of the Panel. It received only 1 vote in favor (Russia), 1 against (Japan), and 13 abstentions (including France and China). France regretted the veto on the first draft and noted Russia's proposal was not discussed. France emphasized the urgency of implementing the peace agreement.

A separate fictional workshop was held to determine an internal review schedule. This session does not reflect official country positions or alter recorded votes. The menu offered four options: A (written note), B (oral briefing), C (oral briefing, open circulation), and D (oral briefing, second cycle).

Current requirements for certification are incomplete. The French workshop drafting desk's requirement remains unknown. The Russian Federation workshop drafting desk requires open paper circulation. The Secretariat technical desk requires a written note. Because the French requirement is unknown, no package can be certified. Furthermore, the known requirements do not exclude every possible package; for instance, if France required open circulation and a written note, package D would be excluded, but other combinations might remain viable. Therefore, the Council cannot certify a package or declare an impasse. Authority is limited to the known constraints of the workshop desks.
